what_it_does: This layer is the substrate that lets any C4ISR application (C2, COP, fusion, PED, AI models) actually reach a military network and stay there. It comprises (1) accredited compute/storage environments at each Impact Level (IL2/IL4/IL5 unclassified-to-CUI, IL6 Secret, and TS/SCI regions) delivered through enterprise cloud vehicles such as JWCC, Army cArmy, and Air Force Cloud One, plus on-prem and tactical-edge compute; (2) DevSecOps platforms and 'software factories' (Platform One's Iron Bank hardened images, Big Bang Kubernetes baseline, Party Bus CI/CD; Kessel Run; Navy Black Pearl/The Forge) that build, scan, sign and deploy containers; (3) the authorization regime (RMF-based ATO, continuous ATO, FedRAMP/DISA provisional authorizations, and the 2025 SWFT and CSRMC reform initiatives) that decides whether software may run on a given network; (4) packaging and delivery tooling for air-gapped, denied/degraded (DDIL) and cross-domain (low-to-high) promotion (Zarf, UDS, Big Bang bundles, CDS-mediated transfers); and (5) marketplaces/app-store-like intake channels (Game Warden, Palantir FedStart, Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace, JWCC/AWS Marketplace listings) that let vendors reach DoD buyers with pre-accredited hosting. Functionally, it is the 'ship-and-stay-authorized' layer between code and the warfighter.

sub_taxonomy.name: Enterprise cloud vehicles and regions (JWCC, cArmy/CAMO, Cloud One, IL2-IL6, Secret/TS regions)
sub_taxonomy.note: Contract vehicles plus accredited regions. Dominated by hyperscalers and integrators; large obligated dollars; JWCC Next is being restructured into a 'Unified Cloud Marketplace' (UCM) with a hyperscaler 'Core' solicitation (Sept 2026) and a second solicitation for non-hyperscaler vendors.

sub_taxonomy.name: DevSecOps platforms / software factories (Platform One, Kessel Run, Black Pearl, Army Software Factory, Space Force factories)
sub_taxonomy.note: Government-owned platforms with contractor support; DoD CIO's State of DevSecOps (Mar 2025) counts 50+ software factories delivering to production. Evidence of consolidation pressure and pivots (Kessel Run 2025) but no single enterprise mandate found.

sub_taxonomy.name: Authorization regime and its automation (RMF/ATO, cATO, FedRAMP reciprocity, SWFT, CSRMC, eMASS/Xacta/GRC, SBOM/scanning)
sub_taxonomy.note: Policy in active flux: cATO memo (Feb 2022) -> SWFT memo (Apr 2025) -> CSRMC tenets (Sept 2025) -> FedRAMP 20x rules (mandatory Jan 2027). This is the sub-layer with the most documented pain and the least settled architecture.

sub_taxonomy.name: Accredited hosting / marketplace intermediaries (Game Warden, Palantir FedStart/PFCS Forward, Tradewinds, AWS Marketplace for JWCC)
sub_taxonomy.note: Commercial 'ATO-as-a-service' hosts that inherit controls so ISVs can deploy in weeks rather than a year; increasingly extending to IL6 and to on-prem/edge (PFCS Forward Feb 2026).

sub_taxonomy.name: Air-gapped / DDIL / cross-domain delivery and day-2 operations (Zarf, UDS, Big Bang at edge, OpenShift/Rancher at edge, CDS-mediated promotion)
sub_taxonomy.note: The least mature sub-layer: open-source tooling exists (Zarf 2.0k stars, actively released Sept 2026) but fleet-scale update, certificate/registry lifecycle and re-accreditation across many disconnected clusters remain largely manual per available evidence (INFERENCE).

sub_taxonomy.name: AI/model deployment and accreditation (GenAI.mil, CDAO, model registries, edge model updates)
sub_taxonomy.note: GenAI.mil delivers frontier models at IL5 in cloud; a formal, repeatable 'model ATO' pathway for edge-deployed models is not documented publicly (Public evidence insufficient).

technical_difficulty.summary: The individual technologies are commodity (Kubernetes, OCI, GitOps, SBOM, scanning, signing). Difficulty is in (a) making the whole chain provably compliant and reproducible under STIG/FIPS constraints, (b) operating it across air gaps and DDIL links with no external control plane, and (c) generating authorization evidence that a human AO will accept and that another AO will reciprocally accept. The hard engineering is distributed-systems reliability under disconnection plus evidence provenance, not novel algorithms.
required_expertise: Kubernetes internals and distribution hardening (RKE2/K3s/OpenShift), GitOps
Supply-chain security: SBOM, signing, provenance, vulnerability triage/VEX
RMF/NIST 800-53, STIG/SRG, FedRAMP, DISA CC SRG impact levels, cATO evidence design
Air-gap packaging and registry/PKI lifecycle (Zarf-class tooling)
Cross-domain solution constraints and classified network operations
Site reliability engineering for many small edge clusters
Federal contracting mechanics (OTAs/CSOs, SBIR, marketplace listings)
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Fleet-scale, auditable day-2 operations for disconnected clusters: pushing image, model and certificate updates to dozens of air-gapped/DDIL nodes, proving what ran where and when, and keeping the authorization boundary valid without persistent reachback (INFERENCE from tooling gaps; no primary DoD document quantifying this was retrievable in-session).
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Container build/scan/sign pipelines (Syft/Grype/Anchore, cosign), Big Bang/UDS Core baselines, OpenShift/Rancher, hyperscaler IL5/IL6 regions, GRC systems (eMASS/Xacta), and SBOM generation are all available off the shelf or open source.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC can run entirely on open-source (Big Bang mirror, UDS Core, Zarf, MITRE SAF) with commercial cloud and no government data. A credible demo needs an IL4/IL5 environment (via Game Warden/FedStart hosting fees or a government software factory sponsor), a signed CRADA/SBIR Phase I-II, and at least one US-person engineer able to handle CUI. First production implies an authorization (own package or inherited), 24/7 support, incident response, likely FedRAMP Moderate/High or IL5 via a host, and possibly cleared staff for IL6; hosting intermediaries charge recurring six-figure-per-year fees (INFERENCE; pricing not public). Ranges are estimates, not quotes.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - the entire stack (Big Bang GitHub mirror, UDS Core, Zarf, OSCAL/SAF, public STIGs) can be prototyped with synthetic workloads and no government data; Iron Bank/repo1 access may require DoD identity for some content.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for the platform itself; required to demonstrate a real ATO package or a real edge deployment (CUI system security plans, network diagrams).
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Pure DevSecOps/deployment tooling is generally EAR (encryption items, e.g., 5D002/ENC) rather than ITAR, but any bundled mission software, CDS components or classified-network artifacts can be ITAR/USML-controlled; a specialist export-control review is required before any non-US person touches deployment artifacts (do not treat this as a legal determination).
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes: ATO packages, SSPs, POA&Ms, network diagrams and most pilot engagements are CUI; DFARS 7012/CMMC will apply to the company handling them.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes for IL6/Secret hosting, cross-domain promotion, and most C4ISR production deployments; facility clearance (FCL) and cleared staff become necessary, which triggers FOCI mitigation if foreign ownership/control exists.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for an unclassified MVP; yes within 12-24 months for any classified/edge production path.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian (non-US-person) co-founder cannot be assumed to access CUI-marked ATO artifacts, export-controlled deployment bundles, or classified environments; a German founder pending US permanent residency is also a non-US person until residency is granted. Company structure (US entity, board control, FOCI mitigation such as SSA/proxy if an FCL is needed), data segregation, and role design (business/product roles kept away from controlled technical data) need specialist legal review (immigration, export control, NISPOM/FOCI). why_not_solved.explanation: Authorization is a human risk-acceptance decision distributed across hundreds of AOs with personal accountability; tools can generate evidence but cannot compel acceptance or reciprocity. Every prior fix (cATO 2022, SWFT 2025, CSRMC 2025) has been a policy change, and policy is still moving, so vendors build to a target that shifts yearly.

Each service runs its own cloud (cArmy, Cloud One, Navy JWCC orders), its own factories (50+), and its own AO chain; a startup must win the same argument repeatedly, which favors incumbents with capture teams.

Platform One (government-owned), Palantir (FedStart/Apollo/PFCS Forward) and hyperscalers already occupy the accredited-hosting and deployment control points; Palantir's Feb 2026 move to IL5/IL6 on-prem/edge and Defense Unicorns' $136M raise show the 'obvious' gaps are being filled by well-capitalized players.
Edge deployment is entangled with program-specific hardware, tactical networks, PKI and CDS approvals; a generic tool without a program sponsor cannot be exercised on real equipment.

Government-owned platforms are free to programs and open source (Big Bang, Zarf, UDS Core, SAF) commoditizes tooling; monetization has therefore concentrated in services (integrators) or in accredited hosting (rent on the ATO), leaving thin room for pure-software startups.
The most painful problems (low-to-high promotion, IL6/TS updates) can only be observed and fixed by cleared, US-person teams inside classified facilities, which excludes most early-stage teams.

For unclassified/IL5 SaaS delivery the problem is substantially solved commercially: Game Warden and FedStart provide inherited controls and marketplace access; JWCC provides regions at every level. The residual gaps are edge/DDIL day-2 operations, cross-domain promotion, evidence automation under a still-changing regime, and model accreditation.

attractiveness.bull: Policy tailwinds are real and dated: SWFT (Apr 2025), CSRMC (Sept 2025), FedRAMP 20x (2026-27) and the JWCC UCM marketplace (2027) all push toward automated, evidence-based, marketplace-style software intake, and DoD is publicly soliciting AI for ATO automation. Open-source building blocks let a two-person team prototype at near-zero cost, and hosting intermediaries let an unclassified MVP reach IL5 without owning an ATO. Defense Unicorns' $136M/$1B+ round proves investors will fund deployment-layer companies with real DoD traction.
attractiveness.bear: The layer is crowded at every profitable control point (hyperscalers, Palantir, Second Front, Defense Unicorns, integrators, GRC vendors) and the customer-owned alternative (Platform One) is free. The regulatory target moves every 12 months, the true buyer (the AO) is not a purchaser, and the hardest residual problems (edge day-2 ops, cross-domain, model accreditation) require US-person, often cleared, hands-on access that this founding team (one non-US person, one pending PR) does not have. Absence of a single dominant edge-ops vendor is not proof of demand.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for this team as a primary bet: attractive as an enabling capability to master (every C4ISR startup must pass through this layer) and as a narrow wedge (evidence automation or edge day-2 ops delivered through an existing host such as Game Warden/FedStart or a P1 partner), but unattractive as a standalone 'ATO platform' or 'tactical cloud' company given incumbency, policy flux and access constraints.

candidate_gaps.title: Auditable day-2 operations for fleets of disconnected/DDIL edge clusters
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Once C2/ISR software is fielded on tactical edge nodes, pushing image, model, certificate and policy updates across many air-gapped or intermittently connected clusters, and proving what ran where for the authorization boundary, is still largely manual and unsupported by enterprise tooling that assumes reachback.
candidate_gaps.user: Signal/G6 platform teams at brigade to corps; software factory SREs supporting fielded units; program offices owning the edge ATO boundary
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Build and scan in a connected factory (P1/UDS). 2) Bundle into an OCI package (Zarf/UDS bundle). 3) Move by approved media or CDS to the target enclave. 4) Manually load into a local registry, hand-run upgrades per node, rotate certs by hand. 5) Manually record what was deployed for the ISSM. 6) Repeat per site with no fleet view.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Zarf/UDS (Defense Unicorns), Big Bang bundles, OpenShift/Rancher with vendor edge managers (Spectro Cloud Palette), Palantir Apollo/PFCS Forward for Palantir-hosted apps; integrator labor for everything else.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Registries, control planes, policy servers and CAs become single points of failure when disconnected; no vendor-neutral fleet update/attestation layer spans JWCC-hosted and edge nodes; continuous-monitoring evidence stops when links drop, so cATO status decays (INFERENCE).

candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-source agent for K3s/RKE2 that records signed deployment state and STIG/scan evidence offline, syncs via any transport (including media), and renders a reconciled fleet view; demo across 5 simulated air-gapped clusters using Big Bang/UDS Core on commodity hardware.

candidate_gaps.title: Regime-agnostic authorization evidence automation for SWFT/CSRMC/FedRAMP 20x
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Programs and ISVs still assemble ATO evidence by hand into eMASS/Xacta while DoD shifts to SBOM-, assessment- and continuous-monitoring-based authorization (SWFT, CSRMC) and FedRAMP moves to 20x, leaving no widely adopted tool that turns pipeline artifacts into AO-acceptable, reciprocally reusable packages.
candidate_gaps.user: ISSM/ISSO and AO staff; software factory compliance leads; ISV compliance engineers
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Engineers export scan/STIG/SBOM outputs from pipelines. 2) Compliance staff map them to 800-53 controls in spreadsheets. 3) Upload narratives and artifacts to eMASS. 4) Assessors validate manually. 5) AO signs; package is rarely accepted as-is by a second AO. 6) Repeat annually or on major change.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: eMASS, Telos Xacta, RegScale/Paramify-class GRC, MITRE SAF/Heimdall and Vulcan (open source), OSCAL tooling (compliance-trestle, GSA fedramp-automation), Second Front/Palantir inheritance for hosted apps, integrator labor.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Tools produce data, not AO acceptance; OSCAL is 'too complex for most teams' (Defense Unicorns retired Lula 1 on this basis); the target regime changed three times in four years (cATO 2022, SWFT 2025, CSRMC 2025) so vendors and programs keep rebuilding mappings.

evidence.claim: DoD CIO memo (Apr 24, 2025) launched SWFT to replace point-in-time ATO with third-party assessments, certified SBOMs and AI-assisted risk review; three RFIs issued and responses reportedly favored continuous authorization.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: CSRMC tenets (Sept 24, 2025) require automation, reciprocity, inheritance and continuous monitoring as the successor to RMF.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Pentagon publicly sought AI to streamline the ATO process (Sept 2025).
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Open-source attempts remain small or abandoned: GovReady continuous-ato-kit (9 stars), Lula 1 in maintenance after OSCAL proved too complex; MITRE SAF (188 stars) and Vulcan (87 stars) are utilities, not an authorization system.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: FedRAMP 20x rules become mandatory Jan 1, 2027 with Rev5 applications ending Jun 11, 2027, forcing every cloud vendor to re-express evidence.
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: The buyer (AO) does not hold budget; the regime keeps changing; GRC incumbents and hosting intermediaries already capture the ISV segment; DoD may build the SWFT back end in-house or via integrators.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High: eMASS successor or SWFT tooling could be government-furnished; GRC vendors can add SBOM/AI features quickly.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Evidence-as-code that is regime-agnostic: a control-mapping and attestation engine that ingests pipeline artifacts (SBOM, scans, STIG results, signatures) once and emits RMF, SWFT 12-characteristic, CSRMC and FedRAMP 20x KSI packages with provenance, aimed first at ISVs onboarding through Game Warden/FedStart-style hosts.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: CLI + web app that takes Syft SBOMs, Grype/Trivy scans and InSpec/CKL results from a Big Bang or UDS pipeline and generates an eMASS-importable package and a SWFT-style vendor attestation, with human review workflow; pilot with 2-3 ISVs already on an accredited host.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Public STIGs/SRGs, NIST catalogs, FedRAMP 20x rules (GitHub); real SSPs are CUI and need a US-person handler.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: eMASS import formats, OSCAL, MITRE OHDF, CI systems (GitLab in P1), host platforms' compliance APIs.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: SBIR topic on AI/ML ATO automation; Tradewinds 'awardable' listing; partnership/marketplace with Second Front or Defense Unicorns; commercial ISV customers first (they pay because ATO delay is their revenue delay).
candidate_gaps.why_now: SWFT and CSRMC created a documented, dated demand for automation; FedRAMP 20x forces re-work industry-wide in 2026-27; AI-assisted narrative generation is newly credible.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Government issues its own SWFT tooling or mandates a specific GRC, collapsing the market; AOs refuse machine-generated packages.

saturation_statement: Research is NOT at saturation. The session's web search budget was exhausted after 18 substantive queries (all results are search-engine summaries with URLs, not full documents); every subsequent WebFetch to government, trade-press, and company domains was egress-blocked (only github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com were reachable); Bigdata.com returned out-of-credits and FMP news was plan-locked.
